parts.title: Learning to do housework
parts.instructions: Read the article and choose the best answer for each question.
parts.passage:
When I left home to study at university, I could hardly boil an egg. My mother had always done everything: she cooked, washed, ironed and cleaned. I had never needed to learn.

The first week in my small flat was a disaster. I put a red sock in the white wash, and all my shirts came out pink. I forgot to switch off the iron and burnt a hole in a table. After two weeks, the sink was full of dirty plates, and my flatmate Ruben politely suggested that we make a timetable.

At first, I thought it was silly, but it worked. On Mondays, I took out the rubbish, and on Wednesdays, I cleaned the bathroom. Ruben did the kitchen, and we shared the shopping. Little by little, I learnt little tricks, like how to remove a stain with salt and how to fold a towel so that it takes up less space.

Now, when I go home for the holidays, I surprise my mother by doing the cooking. She says she can hardly believe it. I think that she is secretly proud.

questions.prompt: What could the writer hardly do when leaving home?
questions.explanation: He could hardly boil an egg.

questions.prompt: What happened with the red sock?
questions.explanation: All his shirts came out pink.

questions.prompt: What did Ruben suggest?
questions.explanation: Ruben politely suggested that they make a timetable.

questions.prompt: What did the writer do on Mondays?
questions.explanation: On Mondays, he took out the rubbish.

questions.prompt: How does his mother feel now?
questions.explanation: She can hardly believe it, and he thinks she is secretly proud.

parts.title: A short history of the vacuum cleaner
parts.instructions: Choose the sentence that fits each gap. There is one extra sentence.
parts.passage:
Cleaning the floor used to be very hard work. [1] People beat their carpets with sticks outside, and the dust flew everywhere.

In the 1860s, a man in the United States invented a machine with a brush that turned as you pushed it. [2] It collected some dust, but it did not remove the dirt that was deep in the carpet.

The real step forward came in 1901. [3] An engineer in London built a huge machine that sucked the dust through a pipe, and it was so big that it had to be pulled by horses.

Later, inventors made smaller machines for the home. [4] In 1908, a caretaker named James Spangler added a bag, which made the machine easier to use.

Today, some vacuum cleaners are small robots. [5] They move around the room on their own and return to their base when the battery is low.
sentences: They do not need anybody to push them.
It was a step in the right direction.
Many people found it too heavy.
It was a completely new idea.
There were no electric machines at all.

gaps.explanation: There were no electric machines at all; the next sentence says people beat carpets.
It collected some dust, so it was a step in the right direction; the next sentence says it did not remove deep dirt.
It was a completely new idea; the next sentence describes the huge machine.
Many people found early machines too heavy; the next sentence says James Spangler improved them.
Robots do not need anybody to push them; the next sentence says they move on their own.

parts.title: Doing the laundry
parts.instructions: Write one word in each gap.
parts.passage: Washing clothes is not difficult, but a few simple rules will help you to avoid problems. First, check the label inside each piece of clothing. It tells you the temperature [1] which you can wash it. Sort your clothes into piles: whites, colours and darks. Wash whites with whites, [2] colours can lose their dye and spoil other clothes. Do not fill the machine completely, or the clothes will not get properly clean. Use the right amount of washing powder: too [3] makes the clothes stiff. When the machine stops, take the clothes out immediately, because wet clothes begin to smell if they stay inside [4] a long time. Hang them up to dry in the sun, if possible, [5] the smell of fresh air is better than any perfume. Finally, fold your clothes neatly, and put them [6] in the cupboard.

gaps.explanation: Because colours can lose their dye.
Because gives the reason for drying in the sun.
Put clothes away means store them in the right place.

parts.title: A guide to the laundry room
parts.instructions: Listen to the talk and complete each note with one word.

turns.speaker: caretaker
turns.text: Welcome to the laundry room, everyone. I am Isaiah, the caretaker. Here are a few rules to remember. The room is open from seven in the morning until ten at night, and you must take your clothes out immediately when the machine stops. There are six washing machines and four dryers. A wash costs two pounds fifty, and you can get a token from my office on the ground floor. Each dryer takes one pound for thirty minutes. Please do not use more than two machines at once, because other residents need to wash their clothes too. If a machine breaks, do not try to fix it. Write the number of the machine on the yellow notice board, and I will repair it. Finally, please remove the dust from the dryer filter after each use.

gaps.explanation: He says the room is open until ten at night.

He says a wash costs two pounds fifty.

gaps.explanation: He says to get a token from his office on the ground floor.

gaps.explanation: He says not to use more than two machines at once.

gaps.prompt: Broken machines are reported on the ___ notice board
gaps.explanation: He says to write the number on the yellow notice board.

parts.title: An interview with a hotel cleaner
parts.instructions: Listen to the interview and choose the correct answer.

turns.speaker: i
turns.text: Onyx, you have worked as a hotel cleaner for twelve years. What is the secret of a good room?

turns.speaker: h
turns.text: Attention to detail. A guest may not see a speck of dust, but they feel it. I always check the corners and the bathroom mirror.

turns.speaker: i
turns.text: How many rooms do you clean in a day?

turns.speaker: h
turns.text: Usually fourteen. Each takes about thirty minutes, so I have little time for breaks.

turns.speaker: i
turns.text: What is the strangest thing you have found?

turns.speaker: h
turns.text: A set of false teeth in a glass, and once a live goldfish in the bath.

turns.speaker: i
turns.text: Are guests generally tidy?

turns.speaker: h
turns.text: Most are, but some leave amazing mess. Once, a group of students left pizza under all the beds.

turns.speaker: i
turns.text: What do you like about the job?

turns.speaker: h
turns.text: It gives me a lot of satisfaction. When the bed is fresh and the room smells clean, I feel proud.

turns.speaker: i
turns.text: Do you clean your own home with the same care?

turns.speaker: h
turns.text: Not at all! After work, I am too tired. My family say the cobbler's children have the worst shoes.
